rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 02] Terminal: Windows Terminal/Linux control behavior

manipulators.description: Ctrl+Shift+N opens a new terminal window
Ctrl+Shift+T opens a new terminal tab

rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 03] Finder: Windows Explorer behavior

manipulators.description: Ctrl+X marks selected Finder items for moving.
Ctrl+V remains a normal paste when no cut is pending.
Enter opens the selected item only when Finder is not editing text.
Delete moves the selected item to Trash.
Backspace navigates back only when Finder is not editing text.

rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 05] Editing and tab exceptions

manipulators.description: Ctrl+F4 closes the active document or tab.

rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 06] Browser and Finder window compatibility

manipulators.description: Alt+F4 closes the current browser window, not just its active tab.
Alt+F4 closes the front Finder window regardless of its tab count.

to.shell_command: /usr/bin/osascript -e 'tell application id "com.apple.finder"' -e 'if (count of Finder windows) > 0 then close front Finder window' -e 'end tell'

manipulators.description: Shift+F5 reloads without cache where supported.
Alt+F4 closes the active window in other apps.

rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 08] Windows key: Start, search, system and window actions

manipulators.description: Win+Space switches the macOS input source using the shortcut discovered during installation.
Tap the left Windows key to open Spotlight.
Tap the right Windows key to open Spotlight.
Win+M minimizes the active app's windows.
Win+Down returns the window to its previous size (macOS 15+).

rules.description: [Windows Keyboard for Mac 09] Screenshots and security

manipulators.description: Print Screen captures the full screen.
Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Force Quit, the closest macOS equivalent to Task Manager.
